review: Independent ordinary correctness review: Windows portability
scope: Exact immutable five-file delta; full surrounding bundle construction, verify, import and cleanup paths; bounded command construction; account validation; actual Windows 82189c4 failure log.
assessment: All eleven recorded Windows failures have a corresponding narrow repair. Eight bundle failures share the unsupported //?/C:/ temporary argument; the other three are an absolute-path fixture assumption and illegal Windows control/quote filename characters.
Only Windows native bundle paths are converted. Unix backslashes remain literal, remote host temporary paths are unchanged, and filesystem creation/read/drop continue using native PathBuf values.

Recognized verbatim drive and UNC prefixes become normal Git drive/UNC spellings while preserving case, Unicode and path components. Generic Win32 device namespaces are rejected. Normal production input is canonicalized before the private directory is added.

Command-local -c core.longpaths=true follows optional --no-lazy-fetch and precedes bundle verify; it does not write user or repository configuration. The same practice-aware/profile-aware bounded command path remains in use.

The private BundleFile value is initialized before path conversion and writing, so conversion/write errors still drop and remove its newly created directory. Success retains the native cleanup path rather than reconstructing it from the Git argument.
Fixture replacements keep Unix control/double-quote coverage and use legal Unicode/metacharacter Windows names; structural quotePath is explicitly enabled.

New tests cover drive, UNC, Unicode, long path spelling and device rejection plus actual over260-byte filesystem creation, exact bundle bytes, Git verification, unchanged destination refs/config, and private directory cleanup. They do not replace actual Windows execution.
